thread:
jordan-pm: Dropped a variant of the rules canvas focusing on density vs discoverability: https://figma.com/file/ABCD. Quick async: which direction is safer for onboarding?

kai-designer: Two layouts: compact stack and expanded cards. Compact shows more rules but hides clause highlights. Expanded makes it easier to scan why a rule matched.

lee-frontend: Performance note: compact virtualized list is cheaper but we lose space for inline condition chips. Expanded increases DOM size; we should lazy-render expanded details.

sam-ux: Usability note: new users prefer explicit "why matched" info. Could we collapse details by default but show an inline cue "Preview Match" that expands inline? Less jarring than modal.

zoe-a11y: Accessibility constraints:
- Expand/collapse must announce state (expanded/collapsed) via aria-expanded.
- Inline "Preview Match" must move focus to the expanded region when opened.
- Ensure the collapse target has an accessible name like "Rule 3 conditions".

jordan-pm: Copy question: current badge reads "No traffic" on unreachable rules. Some feedback called it vague. Alternatives: "No matches", "Rule unreachable" or "Won't match". Thoughts?

kai-designer: "No matches" is concise but bland. "Rule won't match" is more action-oriented. We should pair with a tooltip explaining common causes.

lee-frontend: Backend needs a stable key for these states. I'd like to standardize on `validation_state` + `validation_code`. Example payload:
```
{
  "validation_state": "warn",
  "validation_code": "no_match"
}
```
Design can map warn->yellow badge, error->red, ok->none.

sam-ux: UX rules for badges:
- Inline short label: "No matches"
- Tooltip content: "This rule currently matches no requests. Check conditions, or move it lower in priority. See example patterns."
- Toast language (when user tries to run simulation on all rules): "Some rules won't match any traffic."

zoe-a11y: Contrast for the badge: ensure 4.5:1 on text, add an icon (warning) so it's not color-only. Also when tooltip opens, keyboard users must be able to dismiss with Esc.

kai-designer: Preview behavior debate: modal vs inline panel. Inline lets you keep context but could push other cards. Modal centralizes controls and allows showing top-3 matches with provenance. Which do we prefer?

lee-frontend: Modal is simpler to implement for a first pass (trap focus, sample requests). Inline is nicer long term but needs smart scroll management. Recommend modal V1.

sam-ux: If we do a modal, include a "Jump to rule" action that focuses and highlights the originating rule in the canvas. This keeps context. Also include a small explanation per match: clause (header/body), example snippet.

infra-bot: sim-bot: preview-sim run 2026-01-18T11:12:30Z - sample 50 requests - matches: 8. Top 3: #4(score 0.92): header X; #2(score 0.78): path startswith "/api"; #7(score 0.61): query param foo=bar.

jordan-pm: Good. Modal summary should display that exact bot text and have a copy button. Ops wants that pasted in tickets.

zoe-a11y: When user clicks "Jump to rule" from modal, move focus to the rule and add `aria-live` polite text: "Focused rule 4. Press Shift+F to open details." Also provide a way to close the modal that returns focus to the originating button.

kai-designer: Visual tie-ins: when modal highlights a rule, add a persistent 2px outline + subtle 8% background overlay on the card. Do not rely solely on color (for a11y).

lee-frontend: Reordering: do we keep stable numbering even when a rule is disabled? Ops requested stable numbers for runbooks. My vote: keep numbering stable, show disabled dim + pill. Also we should allow keyboard reordering via lift/drop pattern.

sam-ux: Shortcut suggestion for lift/drop: Enter to pick up, Up/Down to move, Enter to drop. Show the pattern in a tooltip on first use.

zoe-a11y: Announce reorder ops: "Rule 5 moved to position 3" via aria-live. And when pinned rules exist, include pin state in announcements.

kai-designer: Pin feature suggestion: visually show a pin lock and hide drag handle when pinned. But pinning adds cognitive load. If we include it, let's add inline help copy: "Pinned rules are fixed during reorders and simulations."

lee-frontend: Implementation constraints: pinned items will be sticky indices and will need explicit API `pinned: true`. Backend must reject ambiguous reorder requests that violate pin positions.

jordan-pm: Action items: kai iterate figma with modal-first flow + tooltip copy; lee to draft small API spec for `validation_state`, `validation_code`, and `pinned`; zoe to draft a 6-point a11y checklist for the PR; sam to write the modal microcopy and the first-use reorder tooltip. I'll collate and loop back.

jordan-pm: Thanks all. If anyone has quick screenshots of how other platforms label unreachable rules, drop them here.
